lectures.title: Amendment Acts and rules of 2026 and the Kigali Amendment

items: **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992:** granted constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj system.
**97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011:** recognised the right to form cooperative societies under Article 19(1)(c), introduced Article 43B and added Part IXB.
**Article 43B** promotes voluntary formation, autonomy, democratic control and professional management of cooperative societies.

parts.t: Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026
items: **Puisne judges:** raises the number from 33 to 37, excluding the Chief Justice of India.
**Total sanctioned strength:** rises from 34 to 38 judges.
**Principal law amended:** Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956.
**Union Cabinet** approved four additional puisne judges
**Lok Sabha** passed the Bill by voice vote without debate
**Section 2 of the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956** initially permitted 10 judges excluding the CJI, giving a total strength of 11.
**Reason cited by the Government:** increasing case pendency.
**Stated objective:** to improve disposal capacity and speedy justice.
**Aim:** an independent, transparent, efficient and professionally administered tribunal system through a judiciary-led National Tribunals Commission (NTC).
**Introduced by:** Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal.
**Lok Sabha** passed the Bill by voice vote
**Repeals and replaces** the 2021 Act (Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021).
**Coverage:** applies to 16 tribunals, appellate tribunals and authorities, without altering their jurisdiction or adjudicatory powers.
**Role:** central institutional body responsible for appointments and oversight.
**Replaces** the fragmented, predominantly executive-controlled administrative framework under the 2021 Act.
**Tenure:** five years or until age 70, whichever is earlier.

parts.t: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026
items: **Amends** the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957.
**Section 2:** brings mineral-bearing land, defined as land containing minerals under Central parameters, within Central regulatory control.
**Section 9D:** restricts State taxes, cesses and similar levies on mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands, including levies based on mineral quantity, value or royalty.
**States** may impose such levies only under Central conditions or restrictions.
**Past dues:** unpaid or unrecovered State levies for periods before commencement become invalid; amounts already deposited or recovered will not be refunded.
**Section 13:** authorises Central rules prescribing conditions and restrictions for future State levies.
Introduced mandatory auctions, District Mineral Foundation and National Mineral Exploration Trust.
Defined leased area and permitted certain captive lease transfers.
Opened coal and lignite auctions to companies without prior coal-mining experience.
Captive mines could sell up to 50% of annual output after meeting linked end-use requirements.
**Notified by** the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change on 31 March 2026.
**Further amends** the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016.
**The 2026 Rules do not replace the 2016 Rules;** they amend them.

parts.t: Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol
items: **Phase down hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs)**, widely used in refrigeration and air-conditioning.
**HFCs** do not damage the ozone layer, but many have hundreds or thousands of times the warming impact of CO₂ over 100 years.
**Full implementation** could avoid approximately 0.3–0.5°C of global warming by 2100.
It is called a **phase-down**, not a phase-out, because limited HFC use can continue after reductions.
Freeze HFC production and consumption at the agreed baseline
Reduce HFCs by 10% below the baseline
**The limits** are calculated according to the warming impact of the gases.
**Equipment** purchased before the first reductions may remain in use well into the 2030s.
**The Montreal Protocol (1987)** was adopted to phase out CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances.
**Countries** have eliminated nearly 99% of controlled ozone-depleting substances.
**The Federated States of Micronesia and Mauritius** proposed bringing HFCs under the Montreal Protocol in 2009.

lectures.title: Government programmes, schemes and campaigns in news

items: **DDU-GKY:** Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana; launched 25 September 2014 under NRLM.
**DDU-GKY results:** more than 18.47 lakh candidates trained in 800+ job types; over 12.43 lakh secured employment.
**DDU-GKY 2.0:** Ministry of Rural Development; placement-linked skill training for poor rural youth.
**Status:** Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission.
**Training:** courses of 3–12 months for youth aged 15–35.
**Targets for 2026–28:** more than nine lakh candidates' training targets allocated to 31 participating States/UTs.
**October 2026:** around 2,015 training batches for approximately 70,000 rural youth expected to begin across 24 States/UTs.
**Andhra Pradesh** had started training for more than 12,000 candidates in three months.
**Goa** was preparing to start training batches.
**Jammu and Kashmir** had allocated 100% of its assigned targets and commenced training against 91% of the allocation.
